cases.prompt: Design the unit tests for `volume_discount_rate(quantity: int) -> int`, which returns the discount rate in percent for an order line. Classify its risk tier and state the boundary value set you would test.
given: Valid domain: 1 <= quantity <= 100; outside it, raise ValueError.
1..10 maps to 0, 11..50 maps to 5, 51..100 maps to 10 (three distinct valid partitions, not one).
The returned rate directly determines what the customer is charged for the order line.
The function receives int only; None/float inputs are not part of the contract.

cases.prompt: Design the unit tests for `apply_refund(balance_cents: int, refund_cents: int, gateway) -> int`, which refunds money through a payment gateway. Classify its risk tier and state the required boundary values and the interaction contract with the gateway.
given: Valid domain: 1 <= refund_cents <= balance_cents; outside it, raise ValueError without contacting the gateway.
On a valid refund, call gateway.transfer(refund_cents) exactly once, then return balance_cents - refund_cents.
A duplicate transfer call would double-refund real money.
If gateway.transfer raises GatewayError, let it propagate; balance must remain unchanged because nothing was committed before the transfer.
gateway also exposes log(message); logging content or order is not part of the contract.
Example balance for boundary values: balance_cents = 100.

cases.prompt: Review this existing test suite for `volume_discount_rate`. It has 10 separate test methods for interior values 12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, and 48 - all inside the same 11..50 partition, each just asserting rate == 5 - plus 2 tests that call the module's private `_round_to_bracket` helper directly instead of going through the public function. There is no test yet for the 0/1/10/11/50/51/100/101 boundary set. Does this suite need changes?
given: 10 near-identical test methods target interior values of the same 11..50 partition, each asserting only rate == 5.
2 tests call the private helper _round_to_bracket directly.
None of the 12 existing tests covers a boundary value or a different partition.
The suite has no test yet for the 0/1/10/11/50/51/100/101 boundary set.
